Synopsis:
President Trump has publicly accused U.S. oil refiners of price gouging while simultaneously hosting a White House meeting with major refining executives (Marathon, Valero, Chevron, PBF Energy, Delek). The meeting focuses on expanding U.S. refining capacity and managing elevated gasoline prices (~$4+/gallon), which have surged following the U.S.-Iran conflict that began in late February. U.S. refiners posted exceptionally strong Q2 profits ($12.6B combined for Marathon, Phillips 66, Valero) amid disrupted global fuel supplies. The administration is also pursuing increased Venezuelan crude flows to U.S. refineries. The political dynamic is tense — executives face reputational risk attending, but also a rare direct policy access opportunity. Exxon was notably excluded following a prior diplomatic misstep with Trump.
